MAJOR: architect_review_check.py: removing `str(d.get("head_sha")) != head` from the coverage loop means a diff review recorded at an older HEAD can now satisfy the check for a newer HEAD; unless the (unchanged) base-ancestry logic below rigorously proves `reviewed_head..HEAD` is fully covered, this is a stale-review gate bypass with no test asserting the new coverage semantics.

AC text vs HEAD evidence contradiction: the AC (and this delta's store-registry concern, now "no ACCEPTED; NIT-only DEFERRED") forbids ACCEPTED, but the recorded AC verification for BI-PF-1484 states "ACCEPTED capped at 2 per mode" and evidence "passed 2 with HIL approval", yet is marked PASS. Either the policy permits ACCEPTED (AC violated) or the AC verification is not actually checking the AC — Gate 2 certified a self-contradicting record.

excluded_content_check.py: `engineering/design/*.md` validation is header-only (`startswith("# Design Pack")`), so arbitrary content — including fenced code or embedded instructions — passes as long as the first line matches; `docs/BACKLOG-SUMMARY.md` and `docs/documentation-index.html` are accepted with zero content checks. A blocking anti-concealment gate that a one-line prefix defeats is not fail-closed as its docstring claims.

review_budget.py `_material_ok`: one historical `MATERIAL_CHANGE` + `hil_confirmed` decision permanently waives the budget for that mode (no ordering vs the over-budget reviews, no expiry, no re-approval per breach), so the cap is enforce-once-then-open; the approval must be required per breach and post-date the reviews it excuses.
MINOR: core/execution_trail.py: swallowing `PermissionError` on `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` treats a permission failure as lock contention, then potentially `unlink`s a lock owned by another principal — masks real permission problems and weakens cross-user lock integrity.

review-budget.json `grandfather: ["BI-PF-1484","BI-PF-1485"]` self-exempts the very items shipping the control; grandfathering should be date/scope based, not a hardcoded list of the implementing items.

design_pack.py: in single-item mode `--fresh` without a resolvable `item` hits `if a.fresh and not fresh(item)` where `item` may be undefined (NameError); also `_norm` only strips `- **Generated:**`, so any other template/timestamp change makes `--fresh` flaky across machines.
review_budget.py `main`: an item id not found by `backlog.get_epic` yields `{}` → `problems({})` → no evidence rows → silent pass; unknown/stale ids bypass the budget instead of failing closed.

encoding_check.py: `BINARY_EXT ∩ CODE_EXT = ∅`, so `and suffix not in BINARY_EXT` is dead; the real skip is the NUL-in-first-1KB heuristic, which also lets any UTF-8 text file containing a NUL evade encoding validation entirely.

SUMMARY: Solid direction: mode-filtered prior context, base-ancestry validation, design-pack freshness and new budget/excluded-content gates with tests are real improvements.

Top risks: weakened review-freshness check in architect_review_check.py, an AC-verification record that contradicts the "ACCEPTED is not allowed" AC yet passes Gate 2, a bypassable excluded-content gate, and a one-shot MATERIAL_CHANGE waiver that voids the review budget after the first approval.

Recommend: restore or prove the head-coverage semantics with a test, reconcile the ACCEPTED policy vs AC evidence, harden excluded-content validation, and scope MATERIAL_CHANGE approvals per breach before merge.
